October 19 1925

REPORT ON Bolshevist Propaganda Among Sailors With Special Reference
to Efforts to Undermine Loyalty of Members of British Fleet

Made by D. S. Korolkoff Forwarded by J. McEwen C. O. I.

Sir,

Certain circumstantial evidence has been collected
by these Headquarters which tends to prove that propaganda,
inciting Chinese and foreign seamen to declare strikes and in
general to revolt, is being conducted by Bolsheviks in
Shanghai. A branch of the Russian "Agitotdel" (translated
means "Propaganda Department") is said to exist at the
Soviet Consulate and at the present moment is being directed
by Solomon Lazovitch Ville - a Russian Jew, who, in addition,
occupies the position of Acting Soviet Consul-General and
is assisted by Soviet Consular Secretary, Abram Hassis, also
a Russian Jew.

According to unconfirmed information in possession
of these Headquarters, the "Agitotdel" employs numerous
agents of whom the most important is certain Golyanovsky who
possesses a knowledge of both English and Chinese
languages. It is said that Golyanovsky on some occasions during
the recent strike was in communication with Chinese strike
organisations and agitators. He is a journalist by
occupation, representing the Soviet newspapers "Echo",
"Sovietski Sibir" and "Ogonyok" in Russia. Another important
agent of the "Agitotdel" is Peter Solomonvitch Strijevsky, a
Russian Jew, who likewise is reported to have been an active
agitator behind the scenes in the recent strike. Strijevsky is
employed as a clerk in the Shanghai office of the Russian

关于布尔什维克在水手中的宣传活动的报告，特别提及破坏英国舰队成员忠诚度的企图

由 D. S. Korolkoff 撰写，经首席情报官 J. McEwen 转呈

先生：

本总部收集到若干旁证，倾向于证明布尔什维克正在上海开展宣传活动，煽动中外海员宣布罢工并总体上进行反叛。据称，苏联领事馆内设有俄国“Agitotdel”（译意为“宣传部”）的一个分支，目前由 Solomon Lazovitch Ville 领导——此人为一名俄籍犹太人，此外还担任苏联代理总领事一职，并由同样为俄籍犹太人的苏联领事馆秘书 Abram Hassis 协助。

根据本总部掌握的未经证实的消息，“Agitotdel”雇佣了众多代理人，其中最重要的是某位 Golyanovsky，他通晓英语和汉语。据说在最近的罢工期间，Golyanovsky 曾与中国罢工组织和煽动者有过联系。他的职业是记者，代表俄国的《Echo》、《Sovietski Sibir》和《Ogonyok》等苏联报纸。 “Agitotdel”的另一名重要代理人是 Peter Solomonvitch Strijevsky，一名俄籍犹太人，据报他也是在最近罢工中幕后活跃的煽动者。Strijevsky 受雇于俄国

Volunteer Fleet. He speaks English and is known to have
visited the (Thomas) Hanbury Sailors Home in Proadway in the
first week of June of the present year.

The work of disseminating Bolshevik propaganda among
seamen was conducted up till spring of the present year by
Vladimir Nikolaivitch Cherkassoff formerly 1st Secretary of
the Soviet Consulate and by M. J. Greben, Acting Military
Attaché of the said institution, both of whom left Shanghai.
Since then, these Headquarters has not been able to definitely
recognise which of the numerous Russian and Chinese agents in the
employ of "Agitotdel" is especially entrusted with the work of
spreading Bolshevik propaganda among the seamen.

In addition to the foregoing, the following facts,
recorded by these Headquarters, conclusively prove how Bolshevist
propaganda is being disseminated among Chinese and foreign
sailors. At the celebration held in the building of the
Soviet Consulate here on the 7th of November 1924 to
commemorate the anniversary of the Soviet Republic, several
foreigners were among those who attended the ceremony. These
men were unemployed sailors from the Thomas Hanbury Sailor's
Home and were invited by the Soviet authorities to attend for
which it appears they received payment.

During a search conducted by the Shanghai Municipal
Police on the 3rd of July 1925, in the premises of the
Chinese Seamen's Union copies of International Bolshevik
literature in English and German languages also leaflets printed

志愿船队（Volunteer Fleet）上海办事处，担任职员。他会说英语，且已知于今年六月的第一周访问过位于百老汇路（Broadway）的（托马斯）汉伯里海员之家（(Thomas) Hanbury Sailors Home）。

在今年春季之前，向海员传播布尔什维克宣传的工作由前苏联领事馆一等秘书 Vladimir Nikolaivitch Cherkassoff 以及该机构的代理武官 M. J. Greben 进行，这两人均已离开上海。此后，本总部未能明确认定受雇于“Agitotdel”的众多俄中代理人中，究竟是谁特别负责在海员中散布布尔什维克宣传工作。

除上述情况外，本总部记录的以下事实确凿地证明了布尔什维克宣传是如何在中外水手中传播的。1924年11月7日，为纪念苏维埃共和国周年庆典，在本地苏联领事馆大楼举行的庆祝活动中，有几名外国人出席了仪式。这些人是来自托马斯·汉伯里海员之家的失业水手，他们应苏联当局邀请出席，并似乎因此获得了报酬。

1925年7月3日，上海公共租界工部局警务处在中华海员工会会所进行搜查时，查获了英文和德文的国际布尔什维克文献副本，以及印有

    On the 6th of August 1925, small red notices
printed in both English and Chinese languages were posted
throughout the Settlement on telegraph poles. These notices
were issued by the Young Communists' League of China and
had as their object the undermining of the loyalty of British
sailors by appealing to them to refuse being the tools of
Imperialist financiers.    Similar notices, issued in both
the French and Chinese languages by the National Federation
of Young Communists, appealing to the French sailors for a
world revolution and the establishment of the Seamen's Soviet,
were found posted throughout the French Concession on the
same day. ~~These two notices are the work of local Russian~~
~~Bolsheviks.~~
9/10
    From information received from the Shanghai
River Police the S. M. P. learned that a foreign agitator
had been observed on board the motor ship "Canton" on the 9th
of August of this year attempting to incite the Swedish crew of the
aforesaid ship to come out on strike in sympathy with the
Shanghai strikers. He also distributed the Bolshevist leaflets
entitled "The Red Seamen of Asia" to the sailors of said ship.
    In September of the present year an unknown German
agitator made his appearance at the General Hospital at Shanghai
and requested to see some three German patients - inmates of
the hospital. On being admitted he distributed sundry communist

英文标题为《中国海员》（The Chinese Seamen）的传单，后者无疑是俄国青年布尔什维克的作品。
    1925年8月6日，印有中英文的小张红色告示被张贴在整个租界的电线杆上。这些告示由中国共产主义青年团发布，其目的是通过呼吁英国水手拒绝成为帝国主义金融家的工具，来破坏他们的忠诚度。同日，在法租界各处也发现了类似的告示，由全国青年共产主义联合会以法文和中文发布，呼吁法国水手进行世界革命并建立海员苏维埃。 ~~这两份告示是当地俄国~~ ~~布尔什维克的作品。~~
9/10
    从上海水上警察获得的情报中，上海公共租界工部局警务处获悉，今年8月9日，有人观察到一名外国煽动者在机动船“广东”号（Canton）上，试图煽动该船的瑞典船员罢工，以声援上海罢工者。他还向该船的水手分发了题为《亚洲红色海员》的布尔什维克传单。
    今年9月，一名身份不明的德国煽动者出现在上海总医院，要求探望约三名住院的德国病人。获准进入后，他向他们分发了各种共产主义

German patients who is an employee of the "Hamburg America
Line" voluntarily communicated this information to the
administration of his company and subsequently to the Police
and stated that he did not know the mysterious visitor, but
that he is known to the local sailors as the person often
visiting German ships in harbour for the purpose of distributing
reading matter of a communistic nature.

Referring to the case of the two deserters from
H.M.S. "Carlisle", who were arrested by the Shanghai
Municipal Police and handed over to the British Naval
Authorities, these Headquarters consider it possible that,
while the Police have no definite evidence to prove it, the
desertion took place under the influence of Bolshevik
agitators - male and female.

关于 HMS “卡莱尔”号（Carlisle）两名逃兵的案件，这两人已被上海公共租界工部局警务处逮捕并移交给英国海军当局，本总部认为，虽然警方没有确凿证据证明这一点，但此次开小差可能是在男女布尔什维克煽动者的影响下发生的。
